market_holds: Spot $18.84 (sealed baseline 2026-11-17 18:08 UTC). No usable option chain, so the only move anchor is the median of 7 prior reactions, 9.89% (max 20.45%); 4 of the last 7 prints fell, including -20.45% on the Aug 2026 guide cut and -10.54% on the Nov 2025 initial-guide print. The stock bottomed at $13.82 on 2026-09-30 and has risen 36% since (+10.4% over 20 sessions, -2.5% over 5), but it is still 35% below its 52-week high and below the $21.96 close before the August print (Yahoo daily bars). Q4 consensus is about $54.5-55.5M revenue and $0.24-0.27 EPS (Benzinga, Chartmill snippets, undated). That matches the implied Q4 from the cut FY26 guide: $52.7-57.7M revenue, $13.5-16.5M adjusted EBITDA and $0.26-0.30 adjusted EPS, with the midpoint flat year on year against Q4 FY25's $54.9M (my arithmetic from the Q3 release and the 9-month figures). Management already pre-set FY27 at mid-single-digit revenue growth with 100-200bp of margin expansion, about $227-232M on the FY26 base. The detailed FY27 guide is the line the stock trades on. Short interest was 2.85M shares on 2026-10-30, about 16% of Class A shares and 9.7 days to cover, down from 3.49M at end-August (Nasdaq), so some of the rally was covering. The company has bought back more than 20% of its shares since Oct 2024, with about $67M left on the May 2026 $100M program as of Aug 6 and a new $350M revolver since 2026-10-09.
view: This is a guide print with the guide's direction already pre-announced. After the August cut (professional services, mainly a delayed utility CIS project, plus softer transaction and Resolve revenue), the Q4 number is set low enough that consensus sits on the implied guide midpoint. Management said professional services would keep declining year on year in Q4, so a modest revenue shortfall against the midpoint is plausible. Recurring revenue (+8%, ARR $174.1M) and buybacks should hold adjusted EPS inside the range. The reaction will turn on the FY27 range against the pre-announced mid-single-digit growth, on margin, and on whether the utility projects are re-timed again. Against that, four things push opposite ways and I cannot net them with evidence. (1) A 36% rally off the September low means some recovery is now in the price. (2) Short interest of about 16% of the float at 9.7 days to cover magnifies either outcome. (3) Management's record on initial annual guides is poor: Nov 2025 fell 10.5% on a guide called conservative, followed by two cuts. (4) Aggressive buybacks will flatter FY27 EPS guidance. I found no fresh independent data since August: no new state awards or go-lives announced, no insider buying (the only Form 4 is a CFO tax withholding at $14.78 on 2026-09-20), no conference remarks, and no estimate-revision data. Nothing tells me the price is behind on either side.

recommendation.reason: The decisive item, the detailed FY27 guide, was pre-announced in direction (mid-single-digit growth, 100-200bp margin), and the Q4 consensus sits on the implied guide midpoint. I found no dated evidence since August that the price has not absorbed: no contract awards, no insider buying, no new executive remarks, no revision data. The run-up and the high short interest make the move large but give it no direction.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A FY27 revenue range centred at or above about 6% growth with re-timed utility projects behind it, plus a large Q4 buyback, would make this a short squeeze up. A range centred below 4%, or a further slip in professional services or Resolve, would send it back toward the September low.

self_critique: The case for long: the guide direction is known, the stock is still below its pre-August level, short interest is about 16% of the float, and buybacks at $14-17 should make the FY27 EPS guide look good. A clean range could squeeze it 10% or more. The case for short: management has missed or cut repeatedly in FY26, initial annual guides have been wide and badly received, and a 36% rally into the print raises the bar. I hold both and cannot show which one the price underweights, so I stay near 50.
approach_notes: Writing down what the price holds first (implied Q4 against consensus, pre-set FY27, short interest, run-up) was decisive and showed the bar quickly. The 'freshest data first' sources were empty for this small public-sector name (no app, traffic or job signal relevant to a guide print), so the work came down to filings, the tape and the short series.
